With `auto` sizes a FILL child genuinely stretches to its (shrinkable) track and a Hug child keeps content size + alignment. - **ARIA ROLE/STATE maps match the DOM client**: the full `ROLE` set (button… menu, incl. `text`/`img`/`radio`/`spinbutton`/`tablist`/`list`/`grid`/ `region`/`menu`) and the `STATE` semantics (one true `aria-*` per state) are canonical with `lib/typescript/src/classes.ts`. - **Semantic HTML elements from `ROLE` + typography** (spec/OPCODE.md §semantic properties): a semantic role retags a **generic `div`/`span` shell** to its native element — `HEADER`→`<h2>`, `PARAGRAPH`→`<p>`, `LIST`→`<ul>`, `LIST_ITEM`→`<li>`, `SUMMARY`→`<section>`, and the landmarks `BANNER`→ `<header>`, `NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `MAIN`→`<main>`, `CONTENT_INFO`→`<footer>`, `COMPLEMENTARY`→`<aside>`, `ARTICLE`→`<article>`, `SECTION`→`<section>`, `SEARCH`→`<search>`. **Control components keep their native element** and emit no ARIA role from `ROLE` (`BUTTON` stays a `<button>`, `MENU` renders its intrinsic `role="menu"`). **Headings** come from a heading `TEXT_STYLE` typography (LargeTitle…Headline → `<h1>`–`<h5>`, always a heading) or from `ROLE_HEADER` (default `<h2>`); non-heading text defaults to `<span>`. Interactive/control roles are NOT in the catalog (intrinsic to the components); a custom button uses `Button`+`ButtonStyle`. The mapping lives in **`src/role_spec.rs`** (canonical with the DOM client — `pathland-ts-codegen` emits `generated/role-spec.ts`), with the role codes centralized in `pathland_core::constants::role`. - **`TREE::INSERT_CHILD` honors its `C` index** (`u32::MAX` = append), matching the protocol and the DOM client's `insertAt`. - **Event surfacing**: `data-event-listeners` / `data-action-id` / `data-binding-id` attributes. - **Navigation slot attrs** (spec DSL.md §4.5 / MODIFIERS.md): a slot node's `ROUTE` (STRING) renders as `data-pathland-route="<path>"`, its `TRANSITION` hint renders as `data-pathland-transition="<platform|fade|slide|scale>"`, its `NAV_CHROME` (F32 enum) renders `data-pathland-nav-chrome="custom"` when `Custom` (the renderer adds no default chrome), and `NAV_DEPTH` (U32) renders `data-pathland-depth="N"` when deeper than its root so the DOM client can hydrate its default back button from the SSR HTML — the DOM renderer mirrors the route into the URL, may animate a swap, and draws the renderer's own back button (the web has no native navigation container). - `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` handled (days + millis-of-day → date/time). - **Design tokens (spec/TOKENS.md)**: - The naming/length conventions live in **`src/token_spec.rs`** — the single source of truth consumed by the renderer AND by `pathland-ts-codegen`, which emits the DOM client's `lib/typescript/src/generated/tokens-core.ts` (`tokenToCssVar`, `isDarkToken`, `isLengthToken`, `resolveTokenCssRef`). - `PARAMETER::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides are collected per snapshot batch and emitted into the document head as CSS: base (light) tokens as `:root` rules, `dark.*` overrides inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` — the browser resolves the scheme natively, so SSR needs no client scheme. - `DESIGN_TOKEN`-typed `SET_PROPERTY` values resolve at render time to `var(--pl-…)`, with the generative `space.<N>` family resolving to `calc(var(--pl-space-base) * N)` (`Node::token_ref`). - **`STRING`-valued token overrides** (e.g. `font.body.family`): a `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` with `valueType = STRING` resolves the value string from the batch's string section and emits it single-quoted (escaped) as a `:root` rule (or inside the dark media query). - The override rules render inside their own **`<style data-pathland-tokens>`** element in the document head, **after** the built-in block (so their `:root` variables win the cascade and the browser applies them) — matching the JS DOM client's `style[data-pathland-tokens]` element. No overrides → no extra element. - The built-in `:root` tokens use the **canonical spec paths** (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background`, `--pl-color-text-primary`, `--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-border`) so app overrides retheme the renderer. - **Full Tier-1 default coverage**: `--pl-space-base` (light + dark, so the generative `space.<N>` family always resolves), canonical typography (`--pl-font-body-size/weight/family`), the radius scale + `--pl-border-width-thin`, the **shared control core** (`--pl-control-*`, `--pl-button-*`, `--pl-input-*`), and the component tokens (`--pl-toggle-*`, `--pl-slider-*`, `--pl-progress-*`, `--pl-gauge-*`, `--pl-stepper-*`, `--pl-picker-*`, `--pl-menu-*`, `--pl-label-*`, `--pl-size-control-*`), all with light + dark values. `.pathland-*` rules reference the canonical variables, so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` overrides retheme components. - **Forced scheme**: `META::SET_COLOR_SCHEME` sets `data-pathland-scheme` on `<html>`; the platform-dark media rule is scoped to `:root:not([data-pathland-scheme])` and the dark values are repeated under `:root[data-pathland-scheme="dark"]`. Forced light suppresses the media rule. `META::RESET_THEME` clears the batch's overrides. - **Explicit `dark.` references** resolve to the forced-dark variable family (`--pl-dark-…`), so they use the dark value in either scheme. - **Unknown/unresolved token fallback**: `var(--pl-…, unset)` so the renderer's own default styling applies. Base overrides are repeated in the dark scope so they correctly outrank built-in dark defaults (dark override → base override → dark default). ## Built-in HTML base design (`design/`) The built-in stylesheet is now **generated**, not hand-written in `css.rs`: - `design/tokens/{base,semantic,component}` is a three-layer Style Dictionary source (flat DTCG entries). Base literals are compiled into literals and never emitted; semantic + component tokens are emitted in four layers (`:root`, platform-dark media, forced-dark/light scheme selectors, and the `--pl-dark-*` forced-dark family). - `design/html/{reset,components}.css` holds the hand-authored reset and `.pathland-*` rules. Component rules consume `var(--pl-*)` tokens; no design-relevant literal remains (sizes, radii, border widths, durations, z-index, focus rings, opacities). - `design/scripts/{build,dev,check}.mjs` provide build/watch/validation. `check` verifies Tier-1 catalog coverage, layer/reference direction, dark/forced-dark declarations, `$extensions.pathland.internal` markings, and that every `$type: dimension` token is recognized by `token_spec::isLengthToken`. - `design/build/base.css` + `base.css.name` (the SHA-256 content hash, e.g. `base-5f86423db422.css`) are synced to `assets/` by `scripts/sync-design-css.sh` (and `--check` fails on drift). `src/css.rs` embeds both with `include_str!`; `builtin_css()` / `builtin_css_name()` expose them and `STYLE` wraps the bundle in `<style>`. - **External stylesheet mode**: `render_document` stays inline (the library default); `render_document_linked(opcodes, strings, root, css_base)` emits `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{css_base}/{name}">` instead. Token overrides and fit-band rules stay inline after it. The C ABI adds `pathland_html_render_linked`, `pathland_html_base_css`, and - `pathland_html_base_css_name`; the Java shim + Spring/Quarkus starters use + `pathland_html_base_css_name`; the Java port + Spring/Quarkus starters expose them and serve the CSS immutable. An empty base falls back to inline. -- The build is wired into `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven - `refresh-ide` profile, and a CI design job that runs build/check/sync-check. +- The design bundle is wired into the Maven `refresh-ide` profile and a CI + design job that runs build/check/sync-check. ## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist: - **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`), including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment, text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds, hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**. - **`css::STYLE`** is the generated built-in `<style>` block injected by `render_document` (see "Built-in HTML base design" above), containing: - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`), - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`, `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`, `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`, `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/ placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer, - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme` dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/ disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`, focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens; `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so native form controls and the page follow the theme. - **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` / - `_free`, plus `pathland_html_icon_svg`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA - shim). `pathland_html_icon_svg(name)` returns the icon glyph's full `<svg>` + `_free`, plus `pathland_html_icon_svg`) for non-JVM cross-language hosts + (Swift/.NET/…; the JVM uses the pure-Java port). + `pathland_html_icon_svg(name)` returns the icon glyph's full `<svg>` (canonical name → glyph, unknown/extension → the renderer's fallback glyph) — how any host serves `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from ONE Rust source (the DOM client's lazy icon fetch) instead of per-platform static files. The `_tailwind_compile` entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`, `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**. - **The cdylib must be refreshed with `cargo build -p pathland-render-html` - (NOT just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not the `.dylib`) before - `mvn install`**: the jar-embed step only fails on a *missing* dylib, a - *stale* one embeds silently and hosts SSR the old component surface (e.g. a - blank page for a newly-added component like `SIZE_THAT_FITS`). + Non-JVM hosts that embed the cdylib must refresh it with `cargo build -p + pathland-render-html` (not just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not + the shared library). The JVM no longer embeds it; `GoldenConformanceTest` + guards the Java port against golden-fixture drift. - **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values decoded by protocol type (FILL/HUG sentinels, well-known enums, colors, strings, bitmasks); opt-in so default output is unchanged, and comments stay valid HTML (content scrubbed of `--`). ## Cross-renderer conformance (no drift) The **`pathland-html-golden`** crate renders a battery of scenarios to committed fixtures under `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/` (`{name}.plpl` batch bytes + `{name}.html` canonical `render_fragment`). Its `tests/guard.rs` fails if the SSR output changes without the fixtures being regenerated (`cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit`), and the TypeScript `test/ssr-conformance.test.ts` asserts the DOM client reproduces the same DOM from the same batches (fresh-DOM + hydrate-then-delta). The SSR output is the contract both renderers must satisfy. ## Not implemented / gaps - **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (spec/LAYOUT.md §content fitting): aligned — it **alone** has no observable effect (the old `nowrap`+`text-overflow:ellipsis` emission is gone, SSR + TS DOM client); under a `LINE_LIMIT` clamp the renderer tail- ellipsizes via `line-clamp`. Renderer-owned fidelity: CSS cannot place a head/middle ellipsis, so non-Tail modes fall back to the tail ellipsis. - **`DESIGN_TOKEN` property references** cover the directly-mappable subset (colors, font size/weight/family, spacing/padding/content margins, corner radius, opacity, width/height, border width/color, shadow color/x/y/radius). **Parent-path fallback and per-component native control chrome are not implemented in CSS** (see the gaps above). - **Grid/ScrollView/Lazy layout (spec/PRIMITIVES.md §Grid / §ScrollView)**: grids emit `gap` from `SPACING`, equal-`1fr` track templates from the `GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS` constructor properties (columns for GRID/ LAZY_VGRID, rows for LAZY_HGRID + `grid-auto-flow:column`), **`GRID_TRACKS`** per-track specs (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>` → `1fr`/`<pts>px`/ `minmax(<pts>px,1fr)`, taking precedence over the count), and **per-cell alignment** — each cell is wrapped in an auto-placed shell whose `justify-self`/`align-self` is `stretch` for a `FILL`/greedy cell, else the grid `ALIGNMENT` position (default start) — with `justify-items`/ `align-items` on the container. **`GRID_ROW`** (0x1D) rows are flattened with explicit `grid-row`/`grid-column` placement; each row renders as a transparent `<div style="display:contents">` (its id hydrates the DOM client), and a short row leaves trailing columns empty. `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` on a grid are the universal pixel box, never a count. `SCROLLVIEW` is greedy (`flex:1 1 auto;align-self:stretch;overflow:auto`) and renders **only its first child** (the spec-pinned single content). Conformance cases C11–C14 covered by the SSR tests + golden fixtures (incl. the `gridrow` scenario). - `SHAPE` `Path` renders as an SVG placeholder (no path data wire property). - GAUGE/SHAPE visuals are CSS approximations, not pixel-exact. - **Parent-path token fallback is not implemented in CSS**: overriding a parent path (e.g. `font.body`) does not derive leaf variables (`font.body.size`). Override the leaf paths on the web. - **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — no external/webfont loading, so the rendered document makes no network requests for fonts and works offline. An app can still pick its own typeface via a `font.body.family` `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` override (any STRING value, e.g. `"Inter"` if the app hosts it). - Compound token refs cover shadow x/y/radius and border width (the DOM client mirrors them); per-component tokens still style only the component CSS the renderer owns. ## Verified by `cargo test -p pathland-render-html` — 77 headless render tests (components, properties, composite, event attrs, navigation slot route/transition attrs, `days_to_date`, network-decoded frames, inline-all styling, built-in CSS block contents, Inter CDN head links, design tokens: base/dark override CSS, `px` lengths, `DESIGN_TOKEN` refs, generative `space.N`). The built-in CSS tests assert the generated bundle is embedded (reset, tokens, component rules) and that component rules reference the catalog/metadata tokens; the linked-mode tests assert the hashed `<link>` and that the default render remains inline. `cargo test -p pathland-html-golden` — the SSR golden-fixture guard. `npm --prefix design run build && npm --prefix design run check` and `scripts/sync-design-css.sh --check` validate the design pipeline and the committed bundle.

Now Phase 2: Port the HTML renderer to Java. This is a big task. Let me explore thoroughly.

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

/**
 * A fixed-size 16-byte Pathland opcode (little-endian):
 *
 * `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32][B u32][C u32]`
 *
 * The component-named methods preserve the Java record accessor API
 * (`op.category()`, `op.b()`, …) used by the renderers, hosts, and tests.
 */
data class Opcode(
    val category: Int,
    val command: Int,
    val flags: Int,
    val a: Int,
    val b: Int,
    val c: Int,
) {
    fun category(): Int = category
    fun command(): Int = command
    fun flags(): Int = flags
    fun a(): Int = a
    fun b(): Int = b
    fun c(): Int = c

    /** Serialize to the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
    fun toBytes(): ByteArray {
        val out = ByteArray(SIZE)
        out[0] = category.toByte()
        out[1] = command.toByte()
        out[2] = flags.toByte()
        out[3] = (flags ushr 8).toByte()
        writeIntLE(out, 4, a)
        writeIntLE(out, 8, b)
        writeIntLE(out, 12, c)
        return out
    }

    companion object {
        const val SIZE = 16

        /** Deserialize from the 16-byte little-endian wire representation. */
        fun fromBytes(bytes: ByteArray): Opcode {
            require(bytes.size == SIZE) { "opcode must be $SIZE bytes" }
            return Opcode(
                bytes[0].toInt() and 0xFF,
                bytes[1].toInt() and 0xFF,
                (bytes[2].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 4),
                readIntLE(bytes, 8),
                readIntLE(bytes, 12),
            )
        }

        private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArray, offset: Int, value: Int) {
            out[offset] = value.toByte()
            out[offset + 1] = (value ushr 8).toByte()
            out[offset + 2] = (value ushr 16).toByte()
            out[offset + 3] = (value ushr 24).toByte()
        }

        private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
            (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
                ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
                ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
                ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
    }
}

Now, one important issue: the Rust `Node` uses `BTreeMap<u16,u32>` for properties, and iterates sorted by key. This affects:

- `debug` property listing: iterates `node.properties.keys()` in **ascending key order** (BTreeMap). For the debug comments. I need to use a sorted map (TreeMap) to match. Use `TreeMap<Integer,Integer>`.
- `tokens.base/dark` are BTreeMaps (string order) for CSS declarations. Use `TreeMap<String,...>`.

`list_csv`: format whole values with `%.0f` and others with `%.1f`. Rust `format!("{:.0}", value)` and `{:.1}`. Java `String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.0f", value)` and `"%.1f"`. Note Rust's formatting of `-0.0` etc. Should match. Also Rust `format!("{}", v)` for f32 in many places uses shortest representation; Java's `Float.toString` differs in some cases (e.g., Rust prints `4` for 4.0f32? Actually Rust's Display for f32 prints `4` for 4.0). This is critical for byte-identical output! Let me examine: Rust `format!("{v}px")` where v is f32 4.0 → "4px" (Rust Display omits `.0`). Java `String.valueOf(4.0f)` → "4.0". That would break golden tests for spacing etc. I must replicate Rust's f32 Display formatting.

Rust `f32` Display uses the "shortest representation that round-trips" and **omits the decimal point for integral values**? Let me recall: `println!("{}", 4.0f32)` prints `4`. Yes, Rust's Display for floats prints `4` for 4.0 (no `.0`), unlike Debug which prints `4.0`. For `0.5` prints `0.5`. For `1.5` → `1.5`. So I need a `formatF32` that yields Rust Display semantics: if the value is integral (and finite), print integer; else use a shortest round-trip representation. Java's `Float.toString` gives shortest round-trip but includes `.0` for integral. I can strip a trailing `.0` when there's no exponent. But there are subtleties: Rust's Display for large/small numbers uses decimal notation? Rust Display for f32 doesn't use scientific notation; it prints the full decimal expansion (e.g., `1e20` prints `100000000000000000000`). Java's `Float.toString(1e20f)` returns `1.0E20`. That would differ. But in the fixtures, values are small/typical. Also for `format!("{v}")` of 0.5, Java "0.5" matches. For 1.0, strip ".0" → "1". Good.

Also `format!("{size}px")` in text_style_scale uses f32 literals 34.0 etc. → "34px", "700" (weight). Java `Float.toString(34.0f)` = "34.0" → strip → "34". Good. Weight `700.0f` → "700.0" → strip → "700". Good. For `0.3` shadow default it's a literal string. Good.

For `format!("{v}")` where v is e.g. `0.4000000059604645` (from 0.4f32)? Java `Float.toString(0.4f)` = "0.4", Rust Display = "0.4". Good. For `0.1f32`, both "0.1". Good.

For `list_csv`, `{:.0}` and `{:.1}` are fixed-point; Java `String.format(Locale.ROOT, "%.0f", v)` matches (rounding half-up? Rust rounds half-to-even?). Edge cases unlikely in fixtures (0, 640, 700). Fine.

For dates, `format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}")` use `String.format(Locale.ROOT,"%04d-%02d-%02d",...)`.

Slider value: `format!("{min}")` etc. Rust Display strips `.0`, so "0" and "1". Java strip. `value="0.5"`. Good.
Slider fill: `((...)*100).round()` as i32; Rust `f32::round` rounds half away from zero; Java `Math.round(float)` returns int with half-up (toward +inf). For 50 exact, fine. Could use `Math.round`.

Gauge pct: `format!("{pct}%")` → Rust Display, strip `.0`. Use formatF32.
Color hex: `format!("#{:02x}...")`.
Aspect ratio: `format!("{v}")` → formatF32.
Border radius etc.: formatF32.
Opacity: formatF32.
Z-index: `v as i32`.
Dates and time: integer formatting.

Also `style_css` uses `format!("{v}px")` for many; use formatF32.

Also `spacing` etc. in debug: `format_f32` → `format!("{v}")` → formatF32.

Also `window` title/locale escapes.

static String formatF32(float v) {

    String s = Float.toString(v);

}

Now the main HtmlRenderer. Replace the existing Java file. The class currently is `public final class HtmlRenderer` with a nested `NativeRenderHtml` JNA interface and static `instance()`, `tryInstance()`, `isAvailable()`, and methods. I'll rewrite it entirely as a pure Java renderer, keeping the same public API:

- `public static HtmlRenderer instance()`
- `public static HtmlRenderer tryInstance()`
- `public static boolean isAvailable()` → true
- `public String render(ProtocolFrame frame, int root)`
- `public String renderLinked(ProtocolFrame frame, int root, String cssBase)`

I'll remove that test and add golden tests. But to avoid breaking other code, I can remove the method. It's used only in the test. Update test.

- Constructors: private (singleton). But the Rust `HtmlRenderer::new()` is stateless; Java can just have one instance. `instance()` returns singleton; `tryInstance()` same.

I need `strings_str(strings, offset)` and `strings_bytes`, `list_csv`, `list_f32`. Port using byte[].

`AttributedString.decode(bytes)` returns the Java model; catch exceptions.

`Applied`: For `SET_PROPERTY`, `vt = (op.b() >>> 16) & 0xFF` (Rust `(op.b() >> 16) as u8`). Note Java ints are signed; use `>>> 16` then `& 0xFF`. `property = op.b() & 0xFFFF`.

For `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`: `vt = op.b() & 0xFF`; `A=arenaRef path`, `B=valueType`, `C=value`. Rust: `if let Some(path)=strings_str(strings, op.a()) { let vt=(op.b()&0xFF) as u8; let value = if vt==STRING { strings_str(strings, op.c()).map(Str).unwrap_or(U32(0)) } else { TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(U32(op.c())) }; tokens.set(&path, vt, value); }`.

For META: SET_COLOR_SCHEME (a=1 light, 2 dark, else null); RESET_THEME; SET_WINDOW_METADATA (a=field, b=string offset).

`SET_DATE`: date = (op.b(), op.c()).

- `eventAttrs(node)` → ` data-event-listeners="m"` (m is u32; Rust formats `{m}` decimal), ` data-action-id="{a}"`, ` data-binding-id="{b}"`.
- `ariaAttrs(node)`.
- `renderAttributed(AttributedString)`.
- `runStyleCss(List<TextAttribute>)`.
- `debug` comments.

Important: `RenderNode.properties` stores `Integer` values. For `EVENT_LISTENERS` etc., u32. Rust prints `{m}` as u32 (unsigned). In Java, if the value is negative (high bit set), `Integer.toString` would show negative. Rust u32 displays unsigned. Need `Integer.toUnsignedString(m)` for u32 printing. Where used:
- `event_attrs`: `data-event-listeners="{m}"` -> `Integer.toUnsignedString`.
- `data-action-id="{a}"`, `binding-id` -> u32 unsigned.
- `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` -> u32 unsigned.
- `SELECTION` index compare i as u32 == selected; use `Integer.toUnsignedLong`? Simpler compare `i == selected` for small ints.
- `NAV_DEPTH` u32: `node.u32Property(...).max(1)`; display unsigned.
- `LINE_LIMIT` u32.
- `OPTION value="{i}"` i is index.
- `data-pathland-depth`.
- `Color` values printed via rgba (treated as unsigned).
- `data-min`/`data-max` for gauge are floats (f32).
- `STEPPER` min/max/step floats.
- `COLOR_PICKER` color u32 -> hex.
- `SHAPE` color u32.

Rust `u32` stored in `properties` as `u32`; Java `Integer` can be negative. Need to be careful for `rgba` (use `& 0xFFFFFFFFL` as in Format). For `u32_property` used as index, fine.

`checked()` reads `SELECTED` U8; stored as int 0/1.

`roleCode`: `f32::from_bits(bits) as u8` -> `(int) Float.intBitsToFloat(bits) & 0xFF`.

`f32_property` returns float.

Now `event_attrs` prints m with `{m}` (u32). Use `Integer.toUnsignedString(m)`. For action/binding `{a}` u32. Use unsigned.

`aria_attrs`: `ROLE` -> role code; `STATE` codes; `ENABLED` == 0 -> " disabled"; `LABEL` for non-ICON/IMAGE/SLIDER/TEXT_FIELD -> ` aria-label="escaped"`.

`render_attributed`: port `segments()`. I need boundaries from runs and links, sorted/dedup. Then for each consecutive pair with start<end, gather attributes (later wins per property), gather link (later wins). Then substring by byte offsets — Java string substring by **char** indices, not byte offsets! The AttributedString stores UTF-8 byte offsets. Rust slices `&text[byte_start..byte_end]` which is safe because boundaries are valid UTF-8. In Java, I need to convert byte offsets to char offsets. I can build a mapping from UTF-8 byte offset → char index. Since the text may contain multi-byte chars, I'll compute an array `int[] byteToChar` of length bytes+1. Or use a helper `substringUtf8(text, startByte, endByte)`: iterate code points, track byte length until reaching start/end, build the substring. Simpler: precompute `int[] charOffsets` for each byte boundary. But segments can be many; O(n) per segment is okay for tests.

I'll write:
```java
static String utf8Slice(String text, int startByte, int endByte) {
  byte[] bytes = text.getBytes(UTF_8);
  return new String(bytes, startByte, endByte-startByte, UTF_8);
}
```
Since byte offsets are valid boundaries, this is correct and simple. For each segment, `new String(bytes, start, len, UTF_8)`. Precompute `byte[] bytes = value.getText().getBytes(UTF_8)` once. Good.

- COLOR: `color:{rgba};`
- FONT_STYLE: f32 as u8 ==1 → italic

- Others ignored.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="{lang}"{scheme_attr}>
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>{title}</title>
{description}{css_head}{token_style}{fit_style}

Note actual Rust format string uses a line-continuation with `\` after `<head>\n` etc. Let me reconstruct exactly:
```
format!(
    "<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html lang=\"{lang}\"{scheme_attr}>\n<head>\n<meta charset=\"utf-8\">\n\
     <meta name=\"viewport\" content=\"width=device-width, initial-scale=1\">\n\

     {description}{css_head}{token_style}{fit_style}\n</head>\n<body>{body}</body>\n</html>\n",
)
```
The `\` at end of line in Rust string literal strips the newline and leading whitespace of the next line. So the actual string is:
`<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html lang="{lang}"{scheme_attr}>\n<head>\n<meta charset="utf-8">\n<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">\n<title>{title}</title>\n{description}{css_head}{token_style}{fit_style}\n</head>\n<body>{body}</body>\n</html>\n`

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-render-html</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Render HTML</name>
    <description>
        The Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer (dev.pathland.render.html): a
        thin JNA shim over libpathland_render_html (pathland_html_render /
        _render_fragment / _free). Stateless: each call renders
        a full snapshot frame to HTML in one pass. The server-side/remote-projection
        target, usable from Spring Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server. The single
        renderer is the Rust crate reused by every language.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals><goal>test-compile</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust renderer cdylib; absent the
                         dylib, the shim tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Embed the Rust renderer dylib in the jar so it travels with the
                 artifact (JNA extracts it at runtime — no java.library.path needed).
                 Copies the host-platform build into META-INF/native/. Fails loudly
                 when the dylib is missing (the CI rust job builds it; locally run
                 cargo build first). -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>embed-native-renderer</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>
                        <configuration>
                            <target>
                                <!-- Determine the platform library extension. -->
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dylib">
                                    <os family="mac" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dll">
                                    <os family="windows" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".so">
                                    <os family="unix" />
                                </condition>
                                <property name="pathland.native.ext" value="" />

                                <!-- Release builds stage one lib per platform under
                                     target/native/<os>-<arch>/ (the CI matrix) and
                                     this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.
                                     A local build has no staging dir and instead
                                     embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                     META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.host}" property="pathland.native.host.present" />

                                <fail message="No Rust renderer library to embed: neither per-platform libs at ${pathland.native.staging}/<os>-<arch>/ (release) nor the host build at ${pathland.native.host} (local). Build it first: cargo build -p pathland-render-html (in lib/rust).">
                                    <condition>
                                        <and>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.staged" /></not>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>
                                </fail>

                                <mkdir dir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native" />
                                <!-- Release: copy each staged platform dir verbatim. -->
                                <copy todir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native">
                                    <fileset dir="${pathland.native.staging}" includes="*/*" erroronmissingdir="false" />
                                </copy>
                                <!-- Local dev: embed the host lib in the flat layout. -->
                                <copy file="${pathland.native.host}"
                                      tofile="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}"
                                      failonerror="false" />
                            </target>
                        </configuration>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>run</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

display.text:
java-natives:
    name: Build renderer natives (${{ matrix.platform }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: version
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { platform: windows-x86_64, runner: windows-latest }
          - { platform: linux-x86_64, runner: ubuntu-latest }
          - { platform: linux-aarch64, runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm }
          - { platform: macos-aarch64, runner: macos-14 }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Build the renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build --release -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Stage the platform libs
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "${{ matrix.platform }}" in
            windows-*)
              renderer_src="pathland_render_html.dll"; renderer_dst="libpathland_render_html.dll" ;;
            macos-*)
              renderer_src="libpathland_render_html.dylib"; renderer_dst="libpathland_render_html.dylib" ;;
            *)
              renderer_src="libpathland_render_html.so"; renderer_dst="libpathland_render_html.so" ;;
          esac
          renderer_dest="lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}"
          mkdir -p "$renderer_dest"
          cp "lib/rust/target/release/$renderer_src" "$renderer_dest/$renderer_dst"
          ls -la "$renderer_dest"

      - name: Upload the renderer platform lib
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: native-${{ matrix.platform }}
          path: lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/${{ matrix.platform }}/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  java:

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Multi-stage image for the Pathland Quarkus SSR demo (server-side HTML + /ws deltas).
# Build context is the repository root. The Java path is pure JVM (the HTML
# renderer is a Java port), so the image needs no Rust toolchain and the jar
# embeds no native library:
#
#   docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .

# --- Stage 1: the Java reactor + the Quarkus app ---
FROM maven:3.9-eclipse-temurin-17 AS java
WORKDIR /src
# The render-html module copies the generated base design from the Rust crate's
# committed assets; no Rust build is needed.
COPY lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets ./lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets
COPY lib/java ./lib/java
# Include the extension's deployment module in the reactor: the runtime module's
# quarkus-extension-maven-plugin validates its dependencies against it, and it is
# not a Maven dependency of the demo (so -am alone would omit it).
RUN mvn -q -B -f lib/java/pom.xml \
    -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment \
    -am package -Dmaven.test.skip=true

# --- Stage 2: runtime (JRE only) ---
FROM eclipse-temurin:17-jre
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=java /src/lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/target/quarkus-app/ /app/
EXPOSE 8080
ENV QUARKUS_HTTP_PORT=8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-Xms64m", "-Xmx256m", "-jar", "/app/quarkus-run.jar"]

input.content:
# pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The **pure-Java HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a behavioural
port of the Rust `pathland-render-html` crate. Stateless: each call decodes a
self-contained snapshot frame into a transient tree and renders it to HTML in
one pass. No JNA and no cdylib, so a Maven dependency runs on every platform and
under GraalVM native-image. Protocol contract: `spec/`.

## Implemented

- **Pure-Java renderer**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` / `tryInstance()` /
  `isAvailable()` (always true); `render(frame, root)` /
  `renderFragment(frame, root)` / `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a
  self-contained snapshot in one pass. The public API is unchanged from the
  former JNA shim, so `PathlandSession`, Spring, and Quarkus need no changes.
- **Byte-identical Rust output**: `GoldenConformanceTest` renders every
  committed `lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr/*.plpl` fixture and compares the
  fragment to its `.html` fixture byte-for-byte (the same contract the TS DOM
  client asserts), including the delta base/change/result scenario.
- **Full renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
  (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
  attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
  `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, literal colors inline, attributed text, media
  surfaces/controllers, proxy views, grid rows/tracks, fit bands, and
  size-that-fits snapshots.
- **Built-in base design**: the generated `design/build/base.css` (synced into
  the Rust assets) is copied into the jar at build time and inlined by the
  default `render(...)`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
  `renderLinkedDebug(...)` emit a content-hashed
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; `baseCss()` /
  `baseCssName()` expose the renderer-owned bytes for immutable serving.
- **Debug comments**: `renderDebug` / `renderFragmentDebug` prefix every node
  with an HTML comment naming its component and decoded modifiers.

**Last updated:** October 28, 2026

The **server-side / remote-projection HTML renderer**: a **stateless, streaming**
pure function of the opcode stream producing declarative HTML. Each render call
decodes a self-contained snapshot batch into a **transient** map, walks it once,
and emits HTML text out — no retained tree, zero cross-call state (Renderer
Statelessness). Protocol contract: `spec/`.

  like a stack with one child) and lays out the (id-remapped) origin subtree the

  node model and renders non-overlapping `<span style>` runs plus `<a href>`

state.output:
`scripts/sync-design-css.sh` (and `--check` fails on drift). `src/css.rs`
  embeds both with `include_str!`; `builtin_css()` / `builtin_css_name()` expose
  them and `STYLE` wraps the bundle in `<style>`.
- **External stylesheet mode**: `render_document` stays inline (the library
  default); `render_document_linked(opcodes, strings, root, css_base)` emits
  `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{css_base}/{name}">` instead. Token overrides and
  fit-band rules stay inline after it. The C ABI adds
  `pathland_html_render_linked`, `pathland_html_base_css`, and
  `pathland_html_base_css_name`; the Java shim + Spring/Quarkus starters use
  them and serve the CSS immutable. An empty base falls back to inline.
- The build is wired into `scripts/lib.sh` (`build_rust_html`), the Maven
  `refresh-ide` profile, and a CI design job that runs build/check/sync-check.

## Design decision (decision A, September 2026): inline-all + built-in design system

Tailwind is **removed**. The renderer emits **everything inline** as CSS in a
single `style` attribute — no external compiler, no class system, no safelist:

- **All opcode properties render inline** (`style_css()` + `border_style()`),
  including the previously class-based enum surface (alignment, text alignment,
  text case, visible, font style/design, underline/strikethrough, clips-to-bounds,
  hit-testing, invert, truncation). **1 dp = 1 CSS px**.
- **`css::STYLE`** is the generated built-in `<style>` block injected by
  `render_document` (see "Built-in HTML base design" above), containing:
  - a **preflight reset** (vendored from Tailwind CSS, MIT — see
    `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES`),
  - `:root` **design tokens** as CSS custom properties (`--pl-color-primary`,
    `--pl-color-background` (document background), `--pl-color-surface`,
    `--pl-color-text-primary`/`--pl-color-text-secondary`, `--pl-color-border`,
    `--pl-radius-*`, `--pl-font-sans`, `--pl-input-*` (field bg/text/outline/
    placeholder/focus), button tokens), named to match the canonical protocol
    design-token paths so `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` can retheme the renderer,
  - `.pathland-button` (the prettified-button POC, with `prefers-color-scheme`
    dark mode) and `.pathland-*` component defaults (toggle switch, slider, text
    field/editor, stepper, spinner, gauge, menu) — the interactive/hover/focus/
    disabled states that can't be expressed inline. Text fields use a
    Tailwind-style **inset outline** (`outline: 1px solid`, `outline-offset: -1px`,
    focus → `2px`/`-2px` + indigo) instead of a border, with dark-mode tokens;
    `html` sets `color-scheme: light dark` + the `--pl-color-bg` background so
    native form controls and the page follow the theme.
- **`pathland_html_*` cdylib** (`pathland_html_render` / `_render_fragment` /
  `_free`, plus `pathland_html_icon_svg`) for cross-language hosts (Java JNA
  shim). `pathland_html_icon_svg(name)` returns the icon glyph's full `<svg>`
  (canonical name → glyph, unknown/extension → the renderer's fallback glyph) —
  how any host serves `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from ONE Rust source (the
  DOM client's lazy icon fetch) instead of per-platform static files. The
  `_tailwind_compile`
  entry point, `tw.rs`, `tailwind.rs`, `build.rs`, `scripts/fetch-tailwind.mjs`,
  `vendor/`, and the `tailwind-embed` feature are **deleted**.
  **The cdylib must be refreshed with `cargo build -p pathland-render-html`
  (NOT just `cargo test` — tests rebuild the rlib, not the `.dylib`) before
  `mvn install`**: the jar-embed step only fails on a *missing* dylib, a
  *stale* one embeds silently and hosts SSR the old component surface (e.g. a
  blank page for a newly-added component like `SIZE_THAT_FITS`).
- **Debug comments** (`HtmlRenderer::with_debug_comments(true)`; C ABI
  `pathland_html_render_debug` / `_fragment_debug`): every rendered node is
  prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
  applied (`<!-- #1 VStack: spacing=4, alignment=Fill, width=FILL -->`) — values

# Releasing Pathland

Publishing a **GitHub Release** (tagged `vX.Y.Z`) runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, which sets the version from the tag, builds and
publishes every artifact, attaches the built files to the Release, and commits
the version back to `main`:

| Ecosystem | Artifacts | Registry |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Rust | `pathland-core`, `pathland-markdown`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-render-html` | crates.io |
| Java | `dev.pathland:*` libraries (incl. the renderer + view-core native libs for windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64) | Maven Central |

## Versioning (tag-driven)

**The tag drives the version** — no pre-bump commit is needed:

- The workflow writes `X.Y.Z` (from the tag `vX.Y.Z`) into
  `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version` + the intra-workspace
  path-dep pins, via `cargo set-version --workspace`) and
  `lib/java/pom.xml` (via `mvn versions:set`) **in CI**, then publishes.
---
## Release

1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
2. The workflow runs:
   - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
   - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
     crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
   - `java-natives` — build `libpathland_render_html` for windows-x86_64,
     linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64. (The JVM Markdown parser is
     pure Java, so no markdown native is staged for the jars.)
    - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
      `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
      native libs to the GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos

# Deploying the Quarkus SSR demo

Runs the [Pathland Quarkus demo](pathland-quarkus-demo/) (server-side HTML at any
path + live `/ws` deltas) as a container — the application evidence for the Restack
proposal (issue #71, `docs/PREAPPLICATION-TODO.md`).

The image is multi-stage: it builds the Rust HTML renderer and inline-Markdown
cdylibs, embeds them into the Java `pathland-render-html` and `pathland-view-core`
jars, packages the Quarkus app, and runs it on a JRE 17 runtime.

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the embed step needs
the Rust dylib and the Java reactor sources):

```bash
docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

The Rust stage builds `libpathland_render_html.so`; the Java stage copies it into
`lib/rust/target/debug` so the renderer jar-embed step finds it. The JVM inline
Markdown parser is pure Java and needs no native build.

The image's Maven step selects both `pathland-quarkus-demo` and
`pathland-quarkus-deployment`. The deployment module is not a Maven dependency of
the demo, but the runtime extension descriptor validates its dependencies against
it; omitting it makes a fresh (empty `~/.m2`) build fail Quarkus extension
verification.

## Run locally

input.oldString:
The image is multi-stage: it builds the Rust HTML renderer and inline-Markdown
cdylibs, embeds them into the Java `pathland-render-html` and `pathland-view-core`
jars, packages the Quarkus app, and runs it on a JRE 17 runtime.

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the embed step needs
the Rust dylib and the Java reactor sources):

```bash
docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

The Rust stage builds `libpathland_render_html.so`; the Java stage copies it into
`lib/rust/target/debug` so the renderer jar-embed step finds it. The JVM inline
Markdown parser is pure Java and needs no native build.
input.newString:
The image is multi-stage: it builds the Java reactor (the HTML renderer and
inline-Markdown parser are pure-Java ports), packages the Quarkus app, and runs
it on a JRE 17 runtime. No Rust toolchain or native library is needed.

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the Java reactor plus
the generated base-design assets under
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/`):

```bash
docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

Another concern: The Java renderer's `renderDocument` uses `decoded.tokens().schemeOverride` access. Java allows accessing a field of a package-private class in same package. Fine.

Another: `Tokens.Value.fromWire(ValueTypes.U32, 0)` returns a Value; good.

Another: `TokenCssValue` for U8 prints `bits & 0xFF`. Rust `TokenValue::U8(v)` where `from_wire` does `(value & 0xFF) as u8`, then Display prints 0..255. Correct.

Another: `Tokens.declarations` uses `TreeMap` sorted by path, matching BTreeMap. Good.

Another: `fitBandStyles` iteration order: TreeMap by id ascending. Good.

Another: `RenderNode.properties` TreeMap by property id ascending; debug property listing matches BTreeMap. Good.

Another: `RenderDebug.quote` — Rust `{:?}` escapes more characters (e.g., non-printable as `\u{...}`, unicode?). For typical text, matches. The `HtmlRendererTest` debug test passes. Good.

Another: `Format.f32` for e.g. `-0.0` and integral. Good.

Now, the golden test passed for all fixtures, which is strong.

Now update the todo list (for Phase 2). Let me create a new todo list reflecting completion.
